tasks.description: Load the CSV, parse timestamps to datetime, enforce float types for temperature and humidity, and verify 5-minute sampling intervals.
Compute Humidex from temperature and relative humidity and assign comfort categories (e.g., comfortable, some discomfort, great discomfort).
Calculate Thom’s Discomfort Index (DI) using temperature and humidity and label comfort risk levels.
Estimate dew point temperature using the Magnus formula based on temperature and relative humidity.
Compute absolute humidity (g/m^3) from temperature and relative humidity to assess moisture load.
Trigger alerts when comfort indices or raw metrics exceed thresholds (e.g., Humidex > 30, DI > 27, RH > 65%).
Detect anomalies in temperature and humidity using rolling mean and standard deviation (e.g., 6-sample window) and z-score thresholds.
Apply CUSUM to identify sudden step changes in temperature or humidity indicative of system events or faults.
Flag readings where the 5-minute change in temperature or humidity exceeds predefined limits.
Estimate short-term linear trend (slope) of temperature and humidity over a sliding window to capture warming/cooling rates.
Aggregate readings into hourly mean, min, max, and standard deviation for temperature, humidity, and comfort indices.
Forecast the next hour of temperature and humidity using simple exponential smoothing (EWMA) with tunable alpha.
Generate a baseline forecast using persistence (last value) and compare accuracy against EWMA.
Detect potential cooling failures by identifying sustained positive temperature trend with rising humidity over ≥30 minutes.
Flag poor ventilation conditions when dew point or absolute humidity exceeds set thresholds (e.g., dew point > 18°C, AH > 12 g/m^3).
Apply a lightweight 3–5 point moving average to smooth temperature and humidity signals before analysis.
Check for missing values, out-of-range readings, timestamp ordering, and duplicates; log issues for maintenance.
Verify that timestamps are strictly 5 minutes apart and align to expected schedule; flag gaps or drifts.
Compute the total minutes per hour where readings are outside comfort band (e.g., 22–26°C and 30–60% RH or index-based).
Construct compact dictionaries/rows with raw and derived features for efficient SQLite insertion and periodic cloud upload.
